Suslanger

Setting

Suslanger is a small, arid possession of Khadagan. Irrigation supports its farms, while harsh and corrupt authority coexists with criminal networks, smuggling and blackmail. Kir and Kel meet in its slave pen. Their escape leads through estates, thieves’ contacts, the Last Shelter and the search for information about the Joons before military papers provide a way to Gipath. [1, 2, 3, 4]

Kel and the slave pen

Soldiers beat Kir nearly to death. In the slave pen, Kel nurses him back to consciousness, shortens his name to Kir and offers a partnership in escape. He initially hopes to explain the mistake to the authorities; the official instead assigns work according to the prisoners’ abilities. Kel has overheard that an officer possesses a map of the catacombs. They escape and use the underground route to leave the fortress area. Once outside, Kel proposes refuge with an acquaintance who collects spiders. Their relationship begins in this shared dependence: Kir needs her local knowledge, and Kel needs a partner. [2, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10]

Shelter at Rindeil’s estate

Rindeil welcomes Kel and her companion to his estate. Kir’s learning gives them common ground, though the collector’s chief concern remains his spiders. Karim, who manages the household and formerly performed on stage, becomes a source of contacts and rumours about another Joon. Feiruz helps Kir hide his conspicuous face beneath cloth, exploiting the fear of disease. Rindeil’s requests include obtaining a meteorite sample in exchange for a rare specimen for his collection. This period of refuge lets Kir search for information, but its safety depends on the owner’s willingness to risk his household. [11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16]

Zara’s affairs

The merchant Zara is another of Kel’s Suslanger contacts. Her side of the story involves a blackmailer, a threatened caravan and contraband that must be recovered before the authorities inspect it. The conversations distinguish successful recovery from arriving too late; the account of the caravan therefore depends on the outcome of that errand. Later, Zara’s interest in a scholar draws Kir into a scheme against Kehel. These dealings develop alongside the search for a Joon, rather than forming a single inevitable sequence of victories. [17, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24]

Feiruz’s last rescue

Feiruz asks Kir to repay his help by rescuing his imprisoned fiancée Aliya. He dies during the escape. Kel urges the grieving Aliya to avenge him and identifies the man who struck the fatal blow. Kir objects to deliberate revenge, but their companions insist on their code. The death of the prison commandant brings searches across the city. Fearing for his collection, Rindeil withdraws his protection, though he says Kir may return once the danger passes. Aliya then leads Kir and Kel to the Last Shelter and speaks for them before Brother Khatul. [25, 26, 27, 28, 3]

The ring and the brotherhood

Khatul demands an imperial signet ring from a cyclops as a test of trust. Kir brings it back and explains his intention to free his family. He also recognises that the ring does not match the description he has read. Khatul already knows it is false, but asks him to preserve the brotherhood’s belief in the trophy. Membership changes how Brother Smith receives Kir: the smith who refused a stranger now offers his craft. Through Aliya, Kir also searches for the missing Sahilia, rescues her and brings medicine. Sahilia’s recovery matters later, when her forged papers open a route into the army. [29, 30, 31, 32, 33, 34, 35, 36]

Defending the Shelter and the ancient treaty

An imperial scout discovers the Shelter. After fighting the expedition, Khatul proposes placing Wormface bodies at the battlefield to conceal the brotherhood’s involvement. In the depths, Brainripper recognises Kir as a Joon and invokes an ancient treaty. He demands the death of a necromancer disturbing the caves before granting access. Later he calls Kir mentally and offers information for rescuing the Priest of Silence from the necromancers. His account of a human searching for Joon remains gives another lead, though he cannot say where that man now lives. The alliance is reciprocal and conditional, not a promise to answer every question. [37, 38, 39, 40, 41, 42, 43, 44]

The report and the passage to Gipath

Karim’s rumour about the missing red-skinned youth becomes a document recovered from the necromancers. It records transformation and teleportation before the attack on the scholars’ mansion, with Gipath as the destination. Kir decides to follow that Joon. Sahilia supplies enlistment papers, and Kel refuses to be left behind, passing as a young man herself. Sergeant Zairak puts them through military training in Death Canyon. Their performance earns a courier assignment to the Gipath expedition. Sealed orders and a portal pass finally let them leave Suslanger under the authority of the same empire that enslaved them. [16, 45, 46, 36, 47, 48, 49, 4]
